entries.why: Stopped containers and build cache, which `docker system prune` removes. Dangling images go too, but Docker does not report their size separately, so the figure shown counts only containers and build cache and understates the real reclaim. Anonymous volumes are NOT removed - that needs a separate --volumes flag this command does not pass. On Windows the bytes live inside Docker's WSL disk image, which does not shrink by itself: compacting it is a separate step.
entries.regen: Images re-download or rebuild, often many GB. Stopped containers are deleted outright: anything written inside them since they last started is lost and cannot be regenerated.
